newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Macintosh buys German automotive chains.
newsitem.headline: Macintosh buys German automotive chains.

text.p: Dutch retail group Macintosh NV said on Wednesday it had taken over two German automotive goods retailers and also bought a majority stake in their buying and distribution organisation.

Macintosh bought ASZ Fachhandel fuer Freizeitbedarf und Autozubehoer GmbH (ASZ) and Baesch Autovorteile GmbH (BAV). The deal, of which no financial details were given, is effective from January 1 of the current year.
It also bought a 51 percent interest in the buying and distribution firm Palo Partslogistik und System GmbH. The remaining 49 percent of Palo will be bought at a later stage, it added.
"The takeover is expected to contribute to Macintosh Retail Group's profits per share from the year 1999," Macintosh said.
ASZ operates eight shops in Berlin and BAV another 13 in the Koblenz area. Their joint annual turnover is about 40 million guilders and the results are around break-even level.
Macintosh said the shops sell a product range which can be compared with its own unit Halfords, ranging from car parts and accessories to bicycles and mobile telecommunications equipment.
The Dutch group said the takeover was intended to create a basis for Halfords in Germany to secure its long-term growth.
ASZ and BAV will be restructured, which should improve their results, and will eventually be transformed into Halfords outlets. From 1999 the number of shops is expected to be raised.
